entries.description: TeamPCP is a supply chain-focused threat actor active since September 2025 with six publicly documented Shai-Hulud waves. The September 2025 and November 2025 waves were followed in 2026 by attacks against Trivy GitHub Actions, Checkmarx KICS images, LiteLLM, the Asurion-impersonating npm packages (sbxapps, asurion-hub-web, soluto-home-web, asurion-core), the Bitwarden CLI 2026.4.0 hijack on April 22, and the Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 campaign of April 29-30, 2026 (mbt 1.2.48, @cap-js/db-service 2.10.1, @cap-js/postgres 2.2.2, @cap-js/sqlite 2.2.2, intercom-client 7.0.4, PyTorch Lightning 2.6.2/2.6.3). The Bitwarden CLI variant explicitly enumerated authenticated AI coding assistant credentials (Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, Kiro, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI). The Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 4 variant added Claude Code SessionStart hook persistence and VS Code folderOpen tasks, turning poisoned repositories themselves into propagation vectors. Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 5 (May 11, 2026) compromised 170+ npm and PyPI packages across TanStack (@tanstack/*, 42 packages), Mistral AI (mistralai==2.4.6), Guardrails AI (guardrails-ai==0.10.1), UiPath, and OpenSearch via a chained GitHub Actions attack: pull_request_target misconfiguration → cache poisoning → OIDC token extraction from runner /proc/<pid>/mem, producing 404 malicious versions with valid SLSA provenance (first documented case). C2/exfiltration: git-tanstack.com (typosquat), filev2.getsession.org (Session messenger), GitHub API dead drops with Dune-themed branch names, and 83.142.209.194 (PyPI payload delivery). CVE-2026-45321 (CVSS 9.6). Confirmed high-profile victim: OpenAI disclosed May 14, 2026 that two employee devices were breached, with the malware accessing internal source code repositories containing code-signing material; all certificates for iOS, macOS, Windows, and Android apps were rotated. Mini Shai-Hulud Wave 6 (May 19, 2026, the @antv wave) hijacked the npm maintainer account atool ([email protected]) and published 639 malicious versions across 323 unique packages in a ~30-minute automated burst — 558 of those versions across 279 @antv packages (g, g2, g6, x6, l7, s2, f2, g2plot, graphin, data-set, etc.) plus echarts-for-react (~1.1M weekly downloads), timeago.js, size-sensor, and canvas-nest.js. The Wave 6 payload is the same 498 KB obfuscated Bun stealer used in the SAP CAP wave, harvests AWS/GCP/Azure/GitHub/npm/SSH/Kubernetes/Vault/Stripe credentials and DB strings, attempts Docker host-socket escape, and exfiltrates via HTTPS POST to t.m-kosche.com:443/api/public/otel/v1/traces (disguised as OpenTelemetry trace data) with Session P2P at filev2.getsession.org/file/ as fallback. Confirmed by Socket, Microsoft Threat Intelligence (2026-05-20 advisory), Snyk, StepSecurity, safedep, Mend, Akamai, BleepingComputer. The actor's @pcpcats X account was suspended; the group has since hosted operations on a Tor onion site. Total Mini Shai-Hulud footprint: 1,055 malicious versions across 502 unique packages. SOCRadar's August 13 row-level review found 2,188 attributable organization records in the March Trivy/LiteLLM data, with 2,085 ending before the LiteLLM releases; this reframes the 2,500-plus organization and roughly 434,000 CI/CD-file figures as reconstructed potential exposure rather than confirmed LiteLLM compromises.
